newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD information center to reopen.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD information center to reopen.

text.p: A court order which prevented investors from viewing information about soon-to-be-privatized state mining giant CVRD has been revoked, said a spokeswoman for Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES).

Under the privatization rules for Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), a so-called Data Room has been installed in the BNDES building in Rio de Janeiro which makes information about the company available to interested investors.
The BNDES spokeswoman said the Data Room would open its doors on Monday for the first group of investors which had registered to study the material on display.

Last week a federal judge issued the order which effectively closed the Data Room, after deputy Luiz Gushiken of the Workers Party (PT) asked the courts to bar investors from gaining access to the CVRD information.
The CVRD information center came under fire before it even opened Nov 11 to register interested investors.
Days before, CVRD President Francisco Schettino expressed concern that the Data Room contained confidential information, disclosure of which could harm the company's business.
However, the BNDES said it resolved the issue and only displayed information in the Data Room which had been approved by CVRD.
CVRD is to be privatized next year, with an initial 45-percent share block to go on sale in February, followed by an staff share offer and a public offer later in the year.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
